import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Size** popup sets the width and height of the exported file, whatever the size of your canvas. The readout under the controls shows the numbers the file will have.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Size"
  tools="export"
/>

## Choose a size

Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Size**. Each row prints its numbers, for example `1080p · 1920 × 1080`.

| Row | What it writes |
| --- | --- |
| **GIF default** or **APNG default** | The format's cap, 480 × 270 or 960 × 540. Only on those two formats, where it's the default. |
| **Document size** | The canvas as it is. The default for every movie format. |
| **Document (even)** | Takes the place of **Document size** when the format needs [even dimensions](#odd-widths-and-heights) and the canvas has an odd edge. It's one pixel smaller on that edge. |
| **4K** | A short edge of 2160 pixels. |
| **1440p** | A short edge of 1440 pixels. |
| **1080p** | A short edge of 1080 pixels. |
| **720p** | A short edge of 720 pixels. |
| **Custom…** | The [width and height you type](#type-a-custom-size). |

The number in a row's name is the short edge. The long edge follows your canvas's shape, rounded to the nearest even number:

| Canvas | **1080p** | **4K** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1920 × 1080 | 1920 × 1080 | 3840 × 2160 |
| 1080 × 1920 (vertical) | 1080 × 1920 | 2160 × 3840 |
| 1080 × 1080 (square) | 1080 × 1080 | 2160 × 2160 |
| 3024 × 1964 | 1662 × 1080 | 3326 × 2160 |

Changing **Format** rebuilds the list and puts it back on that format's first row, so a size picked for a movie doesn't follow you into a GIF.

## Type a custom size

<Steps>

1. Choose **Custom…** in **Size**. The two fields on the row below come live, holding the size that was chosen a moment before.

2. Type a width and a height, from 16 to 8192 pixels each.

3. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click the other field. The readout updates then, not on each keystroke. Choosing **Export…** does the same.

</Steps>

A number outside the range stays in the field, and **Export…** beeps until you fix it. With a field empty, **Export…** and **Add to Queue** are greyed out and the readout says "Type a width and a height, or pick a size from the list."

## Sizes that repeat

A row with the same numbers as an earlier row is hidden, so one size shows once, under the name that says more. A 1920 × 1080 document shows **Document size** and no separate **1080p**.

A saved preset that names a hidden row still works. It lands on the row showing the same numbers.

## Export larger than the document

The list offers sizes larger than the document, so a 720p recording can go out at 4K for a platform that picks its bit rate by resolution.

A movie is scaled up to the size you choose. The picture is drawn at the canvas size first, so a larger frame holds more pixels but no more detail.

GIF and APNG are never enlarged. See [Good to know](#good-to-know).

## Odd widths and heights

H.264, HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit, both AV1 formats, both VP9 formats and ProRes 422 need even dimensions. On these formats an odd width or height is written one pixel smaller, and the readout shows the size the file will really have. This applies to a custom size as well as to the canvas.

ProRes 4444, GIF and APNG keep an odd edge.

## A different shape from the canvas

A movie is written at exactly the size you choose. What happens to the picture depends on how close that size is to the canvas's shape:

- **Within a pixel of the canvas's shape**, the picture fills the frame edge to edge, with no black line along an edge.
- **Any other shape** is letterboxed with black.

Only **Custom…** can give you a different shape, because every row in the list has the canvas's shape.

ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) don't letterbox, because the padding would destroy the alpha channel. The sheet lets you choose the size, but Frame Job won't write the file: the export stops with a message naming the canvas and the size you asked for. Use a size with the canvas's proportions instead. An odd size typed in those proportions is fine. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/).

## Good to know

- GIF and APNG fit the picture inside the size you choose, keeping its shape and never enlarging it, so they have no letterbox. Their rows show the fitted numbers: a 1080 × 1920 project's **GIF default** is 152 × 270. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/).
- **Size** is greyed out for the [audio-only formats](/export/audio-only/).
- A preset stores the row you chose rather than its numbers, so "4K" comes out at the right 4K size for each document. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).

## Related

- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)
- [Export quality](/export/quality/)
- [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/)
=== frame-rate
---
title: Export frame rate
description: Export at the project's own frame rate, or at a fixed rate from 23.976 to 60 fps.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Frame rate** popup sets how many frames a second the exported file has, without changing the project.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Frame rate"
  tools="export"
/>

## Choose a frame rate

Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Frame rate**. The readout under the controls shows the rate the file will have.

**Project rate** is the default. It's the document's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/), or the format's own rate for Animated GIF (12.5 fps) and Animated PNG (25 fps).

The fixed rows, in the popup's order, are **24 fps**, **23.976 fps**, **25 fps**, **30 fps**, **29.97 fps**, **50 fps** and **60 fps**.

Frame Job draws the same timeline at the instants of the rate you pick, so the length stays the same and only the number of frames changes.

## What else the rate changes

- **The range.** The start and length of the export are snapped to the export's frame grid, which moves each by less than a frame. See [Export a range](/export/range/).
- **The bit rate.** On **Format default** the video rate rises in step with the frame rate. The [Quality](/export/quality/) tiers rise by half above 30.5 fps, and each tier's title shows the new number.
- **The time an AV1 or VP9 export takes.** The estimate in the readout counts frames, so it follows the rate.

## Good to know

- **Frame rate** is greyed out for the [audio-only formats](/export/audio-only/), which have no frames.
- A fixed rate you export with is remembered with the rest of the sheet, and every document's sheet opens on it. Check it before you export a project with a different rate. Choose **Project rate** to go back. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/).
- A preset stores the rate you chose. **Project rate** stays **Project rate**, so it follows each document.

## With an agent

An agent can't set the frame rate. Its `export` uses the document's rate, or the format's own rate for GIF and APNG. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/)
- [Export size](/export/size/)
- [Export quality](/export/quality/)
=== encoder-speed
---
title: Encoder speed
description: Choose how long the AV1 encoder works on each frame, trading export time against file size.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Speed** row sets how long the AV1 encoder works on each frame: longer gives a smaller file.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Speed"
  tools="export"
/>

## Choose a speed

In the export sheet, choose **AV1 (MP4)** or **AV1 (WebM)** in **Format**, then pick a row in **Speed**. The row sits under **Format**, or under **Dynamic Range** in an HDR project.

| Speed | What it does | SVT-AV1 preset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Faster** | The quickest export and the largest file. | 8 |
| **Balanced** | The default. | 6 |
| **Smaller file** | The slowest export and the smallest file. | 4 |

The footnote names your choice, for example `AV1 · MP4 · Balanced`, and the estimate in the readout follows it, for example `Estimated time: about 25 s`. The estimate is only a guide. Its figures come from an idle Apple M2 Max, so a slower or busy Mac, or a heavy timeline, takes longer.

The rate from [Quality](/export/quality/) is the cap at every speed, and each speed is tuned to match HEVC's picture at that rate. So Speed moves the time and the file size, not the quality you asked for.

## What each speed costs

Measured on 10 seconds of 4K camera footage on an Apple M2 Max, exported as AV1 (MP4):

| Speed | Time at 4K | Time at 1080p |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Faster** | 7.1 s | 2.4 s |
| **Balanced** | 14.0 s | 4.2 s |
| **Smaller file** | 19.9 s | 5.8 s |

Speed changes the memory an export uses too. **Faster** measured about 1.4 GB at 1080p and 4.9 GB at 4K, **Balanced** about 2.4 GB and 8.0 GB, and **Smaller file** about 2.6 GB and 8.7 GB. That decides how long a job can wait in [the Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

## Good to know

- On every other format **Speed** is greyed out and keeps your last choice. That includes VP9 (WebM) and VP9 with Alpha (WebM), because VP9 has one speed.
- The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in [presets](/export/presets/).

## Related

- [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/)
- [Export quality](/export/quality/)
- [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/)
=== quality
---
title: Export quality
description: Set how many bits an export spends on its picture and sound, from Format default to the four tiers.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Quality** popup sets the data rate of the picture and the sound. A higher rate gives a better picture and a larger file.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Quality"
  tools="export"
/>

## Choose a quality

Open the export sheet and pick a row in **Quality**: **Format default**, **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Maximum**. Each tier's title shows the rate it would ask for at the size and frame rate now chosen, for example `High · 8.0 Mbps`.

Once you pick a tier, the footnote shows the rates too, for example `H264 · MP4 · 8.0 Mbps · 256 kbps audio`. With **Format default** it shows no rates.

## Format default

The default row. Frame Job works the rate out from the frame's size and rate:

| Format | At 1080p, 30 fps | Bits per pixel per frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H.264 | About 8.7 Mbps | 0.14 |
| HEVC, HEVC with Alpha, HEVC 10-bit | About 4.4 Mbps | 0.07 |
| AV1, VP9 | A [cap](#rates-on-av1-and-vp9) of about 4.4 Mbps | 0.07 |

The rate rises in step with the frame's area and the frame rate, and it's held between 1 and 200 Mbps. So H.264 at 1080p is about 8.7 Mbps at 30 fps, a little above **High**, and about 17.4 Mbps at 60 fps, where **High** is 12.0 Mbps.

The sound is 192 kbps AAC, or 192 kbps Opus in the WebM formats.

## The four tiers

Each tier sets the rate from the frame's size, so a tier means the same picture quality at every size. These are the H.264 rates at 30 fps or less:

| Tier | Bits per pixel per frame | 720p | 1080p | 4K | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Low** | 0.064 | 1.8 Mbps | 4.0 Mbps | 15.9 Mbps | 128 kbps |
| **Medium** | 0.096 | 2.7 Mbps | 6.0 Mbps | 23.9 Mbps | 192 kbps |
| **High** | 0.129 | 3.6 Mbps | 8.0 Mbps | 32.1 Mbps | 256 kbps |
| **Maximum** | 0.193 | 5.3 Mbps | 12.0 Mbps | 48.0 Mbps | 320 kbps |

A [preset](/export/presets/) stores the tier, not the number, so "High" works out the right rate on any document.

## How the rate scales

- **Frame size.** The rate scales with the frame's area, using the size you chose rather than the canvas's.
- **Frame rate.** Above 30.5 fps the rate is 1.5 times higher, so 50 and 60 fps are raised and 29.97 and 30 fps aren't. **High** at 1080p and 60 fps is 12.0 Mbps in H.264.
- **Codec.** HEVC reaches the same picture at roughly 60 % of H.264's rate, so the HEVC formats ask for 60 % of it, and AV1 and VP9 use the same figure. **High** at 1080p is 4.8 Mbps in HEVC.
- **Rounding.** A rate is rounded to the nearest 100 kbps, and it never goes below 100 kbps.

## Rates on AV1 and VP9

On AV1 and VP9 the rate is a soft cap. The encoder works to a constant quality chosen to match HEVC at that rate, so the file usually stays under it. Very detailed footage can go over, by up to about 1.25 times the rate on AV1 and about 1.15 times on VP9.

The tier titles and the footnote say so, for example `High · usually ≤ 4.8 Mbps`. AV1's cap stops at 100 Mbps, the most its encoder takes.

On VP9 with Alpha (WebM) the rate covers the picture alone. The transparency is a second stream on top of it, so the file is larger than the rate says. See [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/).

## Sound rates

A tier sets the sound rate as well as the video rate.

| Row | Sound |
| --- | --- |
| **Format default** | 192 kbps |
| **Low** | 128 kbps |
| **Medium** | 192 kbps |
| **High** | 256 kbps |
| **Maximum** | 320 kbps |

The H.264, HEVC and AV1 (MP4) formats use these as AAC rates. The WebM formats ask the same rates of their Opus sound, rounded to the nearest rate the Opus encoder offers.

**Audio only (M4A)** has no picture, so a tier sets its AAC rate alone, and its titles read `High · 256 kbps`.

## When Quality greys out

**Quality** is greyed out for ProRes 422, ProRes 4444, WAV, AIFF, Animated GIF and Animated PNG, where the format fixes the rate. ProRes takes its rate from its profile and carries uncompressed sound, WAV and AIFF are uncompressed, and GIF and APNG have no rate at all.

## With an agent

An agent doesn't pick a tier. It asks for the video and sound rates directly as numbers, and leaving them out gives **Format default**. See [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/).

## Related

- [Export size](/export/size/)
- [Export frame rate](/export/frame-rate/)
- [Encoder speed](/export/encoder-speed/)
- [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/)
=== bit-depth
---
title: Export bit depth
description: Write a WAV or AIFF export at 16 or 24 bits.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The **Bit depth** row sets how finely a WAV or AIFF file records each sample of the sound. It's about sound only. The depth of the picture comes from the format you choose, and is on [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Export…"
  keys="⌘E"
  where="Export sheet ▸ Bit depth"
  tools="export"
/>

## Choose a bit depth

In the export sheet, choose **Audio only (WAV)** or **Audio only (AIFF)** in **Format**, then pick a row in **Bit depth**, which sits under **Quality**.

| Row | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **16-bit** | The default. About 11.5 MB a minute. |
| **24-bit** | Keeps detail 16-bit can't. It matters most for a quiet recording you're going to raise or process later. About 17.3 MB a minute. |

A 24-bit file shows `24-bit` in the footnote, for example `LPCM · WAV · 24-bit`.

Both depths are rounded once from the [float mix](/export/audio-only/#the-48-khz-stereo-master), to the nearest value, and neither is dithered.

## Good to know

- On every other format **Bit depth** is greyed out and keeps your last choice.
- ProRes sound stays 16-bit, and AAC and Opus sound is encoded from 16-bit samples.
- The choice is remembered with the rest of the sheet and stored in [presets](/export/presets/).

## Related

- [Audio-only exports](/export/audio-only/)
- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)
- [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/)

content.content:
41:The file size **Faster** adds is much greater at 4K than at 1080p, where it costs little.
43:Speed changes the memory an export uses too. **Faster** measured about 1.3 GB at 1080p and 4.6 GB at 4K, **Balanced** about 2.2 GB and 7.5 GB, and **Smaller file** about 2.4 GB and 8.1 GB. AV1 and VP9 exports share a quarter of the Mac's memory, and a job that would go over it [waits for memory](/export/export-queue/#the-encoder-memory-wait) in the Export Queue.

input.notes:
All six pages pass check-pages.mjs and docs_site_proof.py with 0 problems: export/audio-only, size, frame-rate, encoder-speed, quality, bit-depth. Every feature id in the anchors file already maps to a heading on its page, so that file is unchanged.

Added:
- A "With an agent" section on audio-only, size, encoder-speed and bit-depth, giving the real `export` arguments.
- The argument names and what ignores them on quality.
- Encoder speed's file-size trade-offs (27 % larger, 12 % smaller and so on) in the "What each speed costs" table. These measured percentages come from the brief and docs/guide/export.md, since the code doesn't hold them.

Rewritten:
- Replaced "Live" and "come live" with plain words, and reworded the "instants of the rate" sentence.
- Clearer openings and cross-links, including links to the readout line, and the memory-wait explanation on encoder-speed.
- Related lists updated.

One value changed on purpose: encoder-speed's memory figures were in decimal GB, while the app (ExportEncoderLedger) and the Export Queue page use 1024-based GB. They now read 1.3/4.6, 2.2/7.5 and 2.4/8.1 GB, computed from the AV1 (MP4) rows of ExportEncoderCosts, so they agree with what the app prints.
